summary: Armenia is visa-free for a broad range of passports — the EU, UK, US, Russia, Japan, the Gulf states and several other CIS and Latin American countries can stay up to 180 days in a year, and China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay up to 90 days — while most other nationalities can apply online for an e-Visa, and some can also get a visa at the border. A smaller group of nationalities must apply through an embassy with an invitation. From 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, nationals of 111 listed countries who hold a US, EU, Schengen or Gulf residence permit can enter without a visa.

tips.text: According to the UK Foreign Office, Armenia's land borders with Turkey and Azerbaijan are closed; the border with Iran is open to foreign nationals, though this can change at short notice. Overland you can otherwise enter from Georgia, or fly into Yerevan — there are direct flights from Istanbul.
The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel within 5 km of Armenia's entire eastern border with Azerbaijan, and along the M16/H26 road between Ijevan and Noyemberyan, because of border tensions.
The UK Foreign Office warns that hailing taxis on the street risks being scammed for high fares, and calls the GG taxi app a reputable service in Armenia.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Armenia?
faq.answer: Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Russia, Japan, the Gulf states and several other CIS and Latin American countries enter visa-free and can stay up to 180 days in a year; citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay can stay up to 90 days. Most other nationalities can apply online for an e-Visa (21 or 120 days) and some can also get a visa at the border; some nationalities need an invitation and must apply through an embassy. From 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, nationals of 111 listed countries who hold a residence permit from the US, an EU or Schengen state or a Gulf state (the UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait or Oman), valid for at least six months from entry, can enter without a visa for up to 180 days in a year.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Armenia visa-free?
faq.answer: Most visa-waiver nationalities may stay up to 180 days in total within one year. Citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay get up to 90 days under their own agreements.

faq.question: Can I get an Armenian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: For some nationalities. Twenty — including Canada, Mexico, South Africa, Thailand and Türkiye — can get a visitor visa at the border outright, according to the Foreign Ministry. Most other e-Visa nationalities qualify on arrival only if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the EU or Schengen states, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia or Japan, or a residence permit from a Gulf state; Taiwanese passports cannot get one. Applying online in advance at evisa.mfa.am works for all of them.

faq.question: Is the land border between Armenia and Turkey open?
faq.answer: No. According to the UK Foreign Office the land border with Turkey is closed, although there are scheduled direct flights between Yerevan and Istanbul, and the border with Azerbaijan is closed too. To combine Armenia and Turkey in one trip, fly or route overland through Georgia.
